purpose: Install pinned rootless Podman with no sudo into a new prefix and attempt to run this application's workload in containers, to determine whether a matched native-vs-container comparison is possible here, narrowing open_gaps[hosting-services][3] ('no container lane has been run against this workload') and [10] ('no matched native-versus-container application comparison establishes deployment, recovery, isolation or operating-cost superiority').
preregistered: If podman (and its full dependency closure: conmon, crun, uidmap, slirp4netns, fuse-overlayfs, netavark/aardvark-dns) installs from checksum-verified Ubuntu archive packages extracted with no sudo, and a real image pull plus container run succeeds, this application's workload (PostgreSQL + FastAPI) will be run in containers and its backup/kill-recovery/acceptance results compared against the native results already recorded in the paired backup-restore-app-rebuild, migration-up-down-up-data-survival and systemd-run-supervision-kill-restart receipts, with pass/fail, timing and resource use recorded for both lanes. If container image pull or container start is blocked by a privilege this task's no-sudo authorization withholds, the exact blocking error will be recorded and no native-vs-container acceptance comparison will be claimed; the native side alone (already fully evidenced separately) stands as-is.

result: Podman and its full dependency closure install and run cleanly from checksum-verified pinned Ubuntu packages extracted with no sudo: `podman info` works, and (after enabling storage.options.ignore_chown_errors, a documented VFS-driver workaround) a real image pull of docker.io/library/alpine:3.20 succeeds. Actually starting a container is blocked: crun's default OCI-spec devpts mount requests gid=5, which cannot be translated because the available user/group namespace mapping is a single 1:1 identity (obtained via `unshare --map-root-user`, itself needed only because the extracted newuidmap/newgidmap are not setuid-root). This is the same underlying cause as the earlier /etc/shadow chown failure during layer extraction: every operation needing more than one mapped UID/GID fails without a privileged (root-installed, setuid) uidmap. A genuine setuid newuidmap/newgidmap install (`apt install uidmap` as root, or an equivalent privileged install) is the only known fix, and this task's authorization explicitly withholds sudo/root installs. Therefore rootless Podman does NOT fully work here under the no-sudo constraint (open_gaps[3] stays open, refined with this precise, reproducible cause rather than 'not attempted'), and no matched native-vs-container acceptance/backup/kill-recovery comparison (open_gaps[10]) was possible: the container side never reached a runnable state to compare against the fully-evidenced native side (see the paired backup-restore-app-rebuild, migration-up-down-up-data-survival and systemd-run-supervision-kill-restart receipts, all native_proven and passing).

verdict_impact.explanation: Refines open_gaps[3] from 'not attempted' to 'attempted with a precise, reproducible blocking cause (no privileged uidmap available without sudo)', but does not settle it: no container of this application's actual workload (PostgreSQL + FastAPI) ever ran, so gap_index 3's core claim ('no container lane has been run against this workload') remains literally true after this check -- only a generic alpine:3.20 image was attempted, not this workload. open_gaps[10]'s native-vs-container comparison likewise remains fully open, since a failed feasibility attempt with no container ever reaching a runnable state does not constitute a matched comparison, partial or otherwise. Does not support or refute container adoption either way: the native stack's own hosting-services evidence (now including backup/restore, migration reversal and process-kill recovery, all passing) is unaffected and remains the basis for the current 'retain' decision.

limitations: The blocking cause (missing setuid-root newuidmap/newgidmap) is specific to this task's no-sudo authorization, not an inherent Podman limitation; a host where `apt install uidmap` (or an equivalent privileged install) has been run would very likely not hit this exact failure. This receipt establishes the no-sudo outcome only.

No native-vs-container comparison of pass rate, recovery time, isolation boundaries or CPU/memory was possible, since no container in this environment ever reached a running state; the 'otherwise record why not' branch of this unit's instructions applies.

The `unshare --map-root-user` wrapper used to get past the initial namespace-setup failure makes podman itself report rootless: false; this is not true subuid-range rootless operation, only a workaround that avoided real root/sudo throughout.

Docker Engine (the crosswalk's other named container-lane candidate) was not attempted; Podman was chosen first as the more directly 'rootless, no sudo, pinned' fit, and time/budget were not spent on a second container engine once the root cause (privileged uidmap) was identified as authorization-level rather than engine-specific.
Image pull success (alpine:3.20) confirms network, registry-auth-less pull and podman/crun/conmon wiring are otherwise correct; only container start (namespace/mount setup) is blocked.

settles_gap is false, not 'partially': no container of this application's own workload ever ran, so gap_index 3's literal claim ('no container lane has been run against this workload') still holds, and gap_index 10's matched native-vs-container comparison was never possible. Identifying the precise blocking cause is a research contribution to understanding why, not a partial settlement of either gap.
